nodes.label: Graphify usage rules for ClassBot
nodes.rationale: Run `graphify query` before raw grep/search/read so codebase questions use a small scoped subgraph instead of GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output; run `graphify update .` after code changes to keep the graph current at no API cost (AST-only).

nodes.label: Weekly planning rules (one veille/day, two live codings/week)
nodes.norm_label: weekly planning rules (one veille/day, two live codings/week)
nodes.rationale: Veille order follows the week's concept dependencies, never requires a concept from a later programme week, and the week's last day is deliberately a lighter consolidation topic because that day's work is handed in.

nodes.label: AI provider fallback chain
nodes.rationale: Ordered per-class keys (Groq, Gemini, OpenRouter, Cerebras, Mistral, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, DeepSeek, OpenAI-compatible) fall back to the ClassBot's own key, then to Cloudflare Workers AI, so every class keeps working within Cloudflare's free daily neuron budget without a single point of failure.

nodes.label: Claude-assisted assessment workflow (outside the app)
nodes.rationale: Lets a teacher use Claude directly (copy/paste JSON) to generate and grade assessments without giving the AI an API key; exports strip names, Discord ids, GitHub logins and emails so student identity never leaves the dashboard, while a per-student reference (P01, P02...) keeps results matchable on return.

nodes.label: Import from GitHub Watcher (predecessor tool)
nodes.rationale: ClassBot can import an older GitHub Watcher's KV-stored students, briefs, debriefs and forum data once, so a migrating class loses no history; teachers must then disable the Watcher's webhook/cron so nothing posts twice.

nodes.label: Points, scoring and anti-farming rules (RULES)
nodes.rationale: Limited challenge types (multiple choice, complexity, predict the output, find the bug, regex) pay full points for 3 solves/day, half for the next 2, then 0, capped at 150/day, to discourage grinding low-effort challenge types while never limiting write code, SQL, HackerRank problems, or assigned/teacher-given work.

nodes.label: Track vs Programme (two learning layers)
nodes.rationale: The track is kept to one language/practice stack at a time so students never see two languages mixed; the programme (year planning + competency framework) governs projects. Separating them lets switching tracks lose nothing and lets a programme's classes run different briefs while sharing the same concepts.

nodes.label: Live coding template
nodes.rationale: Deliberately small (app.js ~40-60 lines, at most 2 named functions, a 5-step déroulé totaling exactly 45 minutes) because the trainer is at the keyboard while beginner learners code in parallel; anything harder is pushed to an optional 'si le temps le permet' section.

nodes.label: Veille template
nodes.rationale: Shaped to fit a 30-minute learner presentation: 3-5 objectives, a 2-3 part plan, 2-3 reflection questions, and French-first resources (MDN fr, JavaScript.info fr) so links stay real and beginner-appropriate.

nodes.label: Workshop template
nodes.rationale: An extra activity for days without a live coding; learners work in groups of 2-3 while the trainer circulates, which is why the format allows more time (45-60 min) and more déroulé steps (4-6) than a live coding.

nodes.label: Inspiration-only / programme-scope rule
nodes.rationale: Topics listed are ideas, never mandatory; the AI only sees topics matching the week's programme technologies (techOfWeek) and the programme week stays the sole scope, so a later-week topic is never proposed. Topics outside the DWWM programme (blockchain, Web3, zero-knowledge proofs, Salesforce, ServiceNow, WordPress, htmx, microservices, message brokers) were deliberately left out.
